grammar: Fixed greeting.
note: Before another third tone, 你 is pronounced with a rising tone. The annotation retains both lexical third tones.
register: Ordinary greeting between peers.

grammar: Polite expression introducing a question.
register: Polite opener when approaching a teacher or stranger.

grammar: Noun; 你叫什么名字 asks someone's name.
note: 子 has neutral tone in this word.

sentence: 老师：你认识他吗？我：他是我的朋友。
grammar: Verb taking a person as its object.
note: 识 has neutral tone here.

sentence: 老师：这是你的书。我：谢谢！
grammar: Fixed expression of thanks.
note: The second syllable has neutral tone.

grammar: Fixed response to thanks.
note: 不 is pronounced bú before fourth-tone 客; the annotation retains lexical bù. 气 has neutral tone here.

sentence: 同学：这是我的书。我：对不起。
grammar: Fixed apology.
note: 不 has neutral tone within this expression.

grammar: Fixed reassuring response to an apology.
note: 系 has neutral tone in this conversational expression.

grammar: Fixed leave-taking expression.
Language noun; object of 说.
Noun identifying a person's role after 是.
note: 生 has neutral tone in this ordinary conversational reading.

grammar: Noun; object of 看 in a classroom instruction.

sentence: 老师：我说，你写。你明白吗？
grammar: Verb checking whether an instruction is understood.
note: 白 has neutral tone in this word.

grammar: Conventional invitation using 请 plus an action verb.
register: Courteous invitation to enter.

grammar: Adjective used directly as the predicate in a yes/no question.
register: Polite check of a teacher's availability.

grammar: Adjective describing a bodily state after 很.
Adjective describing a bodily state after 很.
Noun in a question identifying an item's owner.
note: 子 has neutral tone; retrieve the complete word 杯子.

grammar: Noun; object of 没有.
Noun; 手机 specifies that this is a mobile phone number.

sentence: 老师，这个字怎么写？请帮忙。
grammar: Verb used in a request without an expressed object.

sentence: 这茶很热，你现在要喝吗？
grammar: Adjective describing the tea's temperature after 很.
Conventional warning.
Verb used as a conventional welcoming expression.
register: Suitable when receiving a visitor.

grammar: Adjective after 很 within a conventional first-meeting formula.
note: 很高兴认识你 means “Nice to meet you.” Learn this surrounding formula as a social chunk.
register: Courteous first meeting.

grammar: Conventional invitation using 请 followed by an action verb.
note: 请 begins with q; 坐 begins with z.
register: Courteous invitation to take a seat.

grammar: Question word before a classifier; 几个 asks how many.
note: 几 begins with j. Its i differs from the vowel represented by i in 字.

sentence: 同学：你要几个杯子？我：四个。
grammar: Numeral before 个; the reply omits the already mentioned 杯子.
note: After s, the spelling i represents a different vowel sound from i in 几.

grammar: Verb taking 你的名字 as its object.
note: 写 begins with x.

grammar: Material noun; object of 有 in a request for writing supplies.
note: 纸 begins with zh. Its i differs from the vowel written i in 几.

grammar: Noun; object of 没有.
note: 铅笔 begins with q; learn both characters as one word.

sentence: 我的字不对，你有橡皮吗？
grammar: Noun; object of 有 in a request for an eraser.
note: 橡皮 begins with x.

grammar: Noun in 这个字, meaning this written character.
note: 字 begins with z. Its i belongs to the z/c/s spelling group; a written character is not necessarily a complete word.

sentence: 老师，我不明白，请再说一次。
grammar: Number plus occurrence classifier; 再说一次 means say it once more.
note: 次 illustrates c followed by the special i spelling. 一 is pronounced yí before fourth-tone 次; the annotation retains lexical yī.
register: Polite request for repetition.

meaning: know a fact or piece of information
grammar: Verb taking the information known as its object.
note: 知 illustrates zh followed by i. 道 has neutral tone in this conversational reading.

grammar: Conventional verb–object expression for having a meal.
note: 吃 illustrates ch followed by the special i spelling.

grammar: Noun referring to prepared food; 这菜 means this dish.
note: 菜 begins with c, contrasting with ch in 吃饭.

grammar: Noun; object of 要 in a drink choice.
note: 水 begins with sh.

grammar: Verb–object expression used after 请.
note: 洗 begins with x and 手 with sh. Before third-tone 手, 洗 is pronounced with a rising tone; the annotation retains lexical third tones.

grammar: Place noun; 在哪儿 asks its location.
note: 厕 begins with c and 所 with s.
register: Ordinary practical question with a polite opener.

grammar: Verb–object expression after 要, stating an immediate intention.
note: 刷 begins with sh.
register: Informal exchange about an everyday routine.

sentence: 我们现在上课，请看课本。
grammar: Conventional verb–object expression for having a lesson.
note: 上 begins with sh; learn 上课 as a complete expression.
register: Teacher announcing the start of a lesson.

sentence: 我们现在休息，你要喝水吗？
grammar: Verb used without an object.
note: Both syllables begin with x. 息 has neutral tone in this conversational reading.

sentence: 我找老师。老师在这里吗？
grammar: Verb taking the person sought as its object.
note: 找 begins with zh.

sentence: 同学：你去哪儿？我：我去学校。
grammar: Place noun following 去 to name a destination.
note: Both syllables begin with x.

grammar: Adjective used adverbially in 认真听, meaning listen attentively.
note: 认 begins with Mandarin r and 真 with zh.
register: Normal teacher-to-student instruction.

grammar: Noun; object of 写.
note: 日 illustrates r followed by the special i spelling. Its vowel differs from the i in 记 within the same word.

sentence: 你现在有时间吗？请帮忙。
grammar: Noun; 有时间 asks whether someone has time available.
note: 时 illustrates sh followed by the special i spelling; 间 begins with j.
register: Direct request to a peer after checking availability.

sentence: 请问，谁是司机？我们要去学校。
grammar: Occupation noun after 是 in a question identifying a person.
note: The i after s in 司 differs from the i after j in 机.
register: Polite question while arranging a ride.

sentence: 我们要去学校，这里有出租车吗？
grammar: Noun; object of 有 in a question about available transport.
note: 出租车 contains ch, z and ch in sequence; retrieve the complete word.

sentence: 同学：你要喝什么？我：绿茶，谢谢。
grammar: Noun naming the drink requested in a short reply.
note: 绿 contains ü; keep its two dots in Pinyin.

grammar: Noun naming the item sought before class.
note: 书 contains u, contrasting with ü in 绿茶.

grammar: Verb after 要; the preceding clause identifies the drink.
note: 喝 contains the final e.

grammar: Material noun after 有 in a warning.
note: 玻 illustrates the Pinyin final o. 璃 has neutral tone in this word.

grammar: Verb–object expression used after 请.
note: 穿 contains uan.

sentence: 同学：你要吃什么？我：我要水果。
grammar: Noun after 要, naming the food requested.
note: 果 contains uo. Before third-tone 果, 水 is pronounced with a rising tone; the annotation retains lexical third tones.

grammar: Food noun after 是 in a question identifying a dish.
note: 豆 contains ou; 腐 has neutral tone here.

grammar: Meal noun modified by 今天的.
note: Both syllables contain an.

sentence: 你饿吗？这里有饭，也有汤。
grammar: Food noun after 也有, adding another available item.
note: 汤 contains ang, contrasting with an in 晚饭.

grammar: Noun modified by 学校的 in a location question.
note: 门 contains en.

sentence: 同学：你热吗？我：不，我很冷。
grammar: Adjective after 很 describing the speaker's bodily state.
note: 冷 contains eng, contrasting with en in 门.

grammar: Noun identifying something to read.
note: 信 contains in. The request to read establishes its meaning as a written letter.

grammar: Verb used after 请 to direct attention to speech.
note: 听 contains ing, contrasting with in in 信.
register: Ordinary classroom instruction.

grammar: Food noun; object of 吃 in an offer.
note: 面 contains ian.

grammar: Adjective after 很 describing the food's aroma.
note: 香 contains iang. The food description selects the aroma word among characters pronounced xiāng.

sentence: 饭馆在哪儿？我们要吃饭。
grammar: Place noun in a location question motivated by a meal.
note: 饭 contains an; 馆 contains uan.

sentence: 这两个男生是你的同学吗？
grammar: Person noun after 两个 in a question identifying classmates; the noun has no plural ending.
note: 男 contains an; 生 contains eng and retains first tone in this word.

sentence: 老师：女生，请读；男生，请听。
grammar: Person noun used to address the group assigned to read aloud.
note: 女 contains ü, with both dots retained after n. 生 retains first tone.
register: Teacher assigning reading and listening roles to two classroom groups.

sentence: 我现在要休息，床在哪儿？
grammar: Noun naming the item sought for resting.
note: 床 contains uang, contrasting with uan in 穿鞋.

grammar: Noun in a correction using 不是…，是….
note: 窗 contains uang. 户 has neutral tone in this word.

grammar: Verb taking the person waited for as its object.
note: 等 contains eng. Before third-tone 我, it is pronounced with a rising tone; the annotation retains lexical děng.

grammar: Verb–object expression used in a classroom request.
note: 关 contains uan; 门 contains en.

grammar: Noun after 没有, naming the resource the speaker lacks.
note: 钱 contains ian. Lacking money while hungry supplies context for selecting 钱 among characters pronounced qián.

sentence: 这里有商店吗？我要面包。
grammar: Place noun after 有 in a question about nearby shopping.
note: 商 contains ang; 店 contains ian.

grammar: Place noun serving as the subject of a temperature description.
note: 厨 contains u; 房 contains ang.

sentence: 老师：现在开始，请看课本。
grammar: Verb announcing the start of an activity.
note: 开始 combines lexical first and third tones.
register: Teacher beginning a classroom activity.

grammar: Verb used after 请; the following question supplies what to answer.
note: Both syllables have lexical second tone.
register: Ordinary classroom instruction.

sentence: 老师，我有问题：这个字怎么读？
grammar: Noun after 有; the following question explains what the learner wants to ask.
note: 问题 combines fourth and second tones.

sentence: 请问，你的老师叫什么名字？
grammar: Person noun modified by 你的.
note: Before first-tone 师, third-tone 老 normally stays low without a final rise. The annotation retains lexical lǎo.

sentence: 请起床，我们现在要去学校。
grammar: Conventional verb–object expression used after 请.
note: Before second-tone 床, third-tone 起 normally stays low without a final rise. The annotation retains lexical qǐ.
register: A courteous prompt to someone who needs to get up.

sentence: 我现在要打字，手机在哪儿？
grammar: Conventional verb–object expression after 要, stating an immediate intention.
note: Before fourth-tone 字, third-tone 打 normally stays low without a final rise. The annotation retains lexical dǎ.

grammar: Person noun modified by 商店的; 在吗 asks whether the person is present.
note: 老 is pronounced with a rising tone before third-tone 板. 板 normally stays low before fourth-tone 在; the annotation retains both lexical third tones.
register: Polite inquiry about a shop's proprietor. 老板 here identifies the owner, rather than any shop employee.

grammar: Short formula seeking agreement with the preceding suggestion.
note: 吗 has neutral tone and is lighter than 好.
register: Friendly suggestion to a peer.

grammar: Adverb before the action 读课本.
note: 一 is pronounced yì before third-tone 起. 起 normally stays low before second-tone 读; the annotation retains lexical tones.

sentence: 请等一会儿，老师现在很忙。
grammar: Short duration expression following 等; 等一会儿 means wait a little while.
note: 一 is pronounced yí before fourth-tone 会. 儿 adds an r-colored ending to 会, not a separate syllable; the annotation retains lexical yī.
register: Courteous request to wait.

grammar: Small-quantity expression before the substance noun 水.
note: 一 is pronounced yì before lexical third-tone 点. In connected 一点儿水, 点儿 rises before third-tone 水. 儿 adds an r-colored ending, not a syllable; the annotation retains lexical tones.

sentence: 同学：你要橡皮吗？我：不用，谢谢，我有。
grammar: Conventional reply declining an offered item because it is not needed.
note: 不 is pronounced bú before fourth-tone 用; the annotation retains lexical bù.
register: Courteous refusal of an offered eraser, followed by thanks and an explanation.

grammar: Conventional reassuring response using 不 with the adjective 急.
note: Before second-tone 急, 不 retains its fourth tone.
register: Reassurance to a peer who needs more time.

grammar: Reduplicated verb in the bounded request 请看看, meaning please have a look.
note: The second 看 is short and neutral in this request.

sentence: 这里有书包，也有手机。这都是你的东西吗？
grammar: Noun referring collectively to the items being identified; 都 asks about all the mentioned items.
note: 西 is neutral in the word meaning things or belongings.

sentence: 欢迎！我的朋友也在这里。
grammar: Person noun modified by 我的.
note: 友 is neutral in this conversational reading, following second-tone 朋.
register: Welcoming a visitor.

grammar: Noun naming an available seat after 有.
note: 子 is neutral after lexical third-tone 椅; retrieve both characters as one word.

grammar: Noun in 是什么意思, the bounded formula asking what something means.
note: 思 is neutral after fourth-tone 意.

sentence: 老师，我不明白，请慢点儿说。
grammar: Manner chunk in the memorized request 请慢点儿说, meaning please speak a little more slowly.
note: Say 慢点儿说 as a connected phrase without pausing before 说. 点 normally stays low before first-tone 说; 儿 adds an r-colored ending, not a separate syllable.
register: Polite request to adjust speaking speed.

sentence: 老师在学校吗？我要找她。
grammar: Location verb followed by 学校.
note: The school-location question selects 在. 再, meaning again, has the same pronunciation zài.

sentence: 这个字不对，请再写一次。
grammar: Adverb before 写, requesting another attempt.
note: The incorrect character and the request to write once more select 再. 在, meaning be at, is also pronounced zài.
register: Teacher or peer requesting a correction.

sentence: 这个男生是谁？他是你的朋友吗？
grammar: Third-person pronoun referring back to 这个男生.
note: 他 and 她 are both pronounced tā. The visible reference to a male student selects 他.

sentence: 我找那个女生，她在哪儿？
grammar: Third-person pronoun referring back to 那个女生.
note: The visible reference to a female student selects 她. Its pronunciation is identical to 他: tā.

sentence: 同学：你要什么水果？我：苹果，谢谢。
grammar: Fruit noun naming the requested kind in a short reply.
note: 苹果 combines second and third tones; the first syllable is lexically second tone.

sentence: 老师：我们现在听写。我说，你写。
grammar: Verb naming the classroom activity explained by 我说，你写.
note: 听写 is one word with first and third tones; 写 is part of the activity name here.
register: Teacher introducing dictation.
